ui.orgSub: Innovation proposals for developing the technopark · 2026
ui.coverLead: From an equipment centre to a self-financing platform that brings together youth startups, regional enterprises, universities and investors.
ui.tocLead: Each proposal comes with its scope, implementation mechanism, timeline, partners and measurable outcome.
ui.roadmapCardDesc: Q4 2026 — 2028: timelines, responsible parties and target indicators.
ui.stateTitleB: a clear solution to each problem
ui.stateLead: Based on the technopark's survey responses. A new proposal addresses each identified problem.
problems: No registry of enterprises' technology challenges and orders
No pilot testing or independent expert reviews; 9 prototypes still at mock-up stage
No reported results in technology transfer
Mature startups show little interest in staying at the technopark
Funding relies solely on rent and production services
Outreach is largely limited to urban youth
ui.roadmapLead: Dark shade — launch quarter; light shade — ongoing activity.
ui.kpiLead: “Now” — technopark survey data; “—” indicates no data reported.
ui.finalLead: By the end of 2028, the technopark will become the Fergana Valley's leading centre for artificial intelligence, textile technology and the digitalization of crafts.
phases: KPI dashboard, advisory board, mentor network, maker membership — 8 proposals
AI Hub, TextileTech, Startup Studio, Angels club — 22 proposals
Fergana Valley hub for AI and industrial innovation

directions.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies
directions.desc: AI services, small business digitalization, IoT and AI education in schools.

items.title: Establish “Namangan AI Hub” at the technopark — a centre for practical AI adoption
items.what: The centre will offer ready-made AI solutions to regional SMEs on an AI-as-a-Service basis: computer-vision detection of fabric and stitching defects in textile plants, Uzbek-language chatbots and voice assistants for retail and service businesses, document workflow automation, and sales forecasting.
how: Form 3–5 “AI teams” of students and startup members, each assigned a mentor
Run pilots at no fewer than 5 enterprises each quarter, documenting results with before/after metrics
Develop a transparent price list and a standard service contract
items.result: Jobs for young people based on real orders, lower costs for enterprises, and a sustainable revenue stream for the technopark.
items.partners: Technopark, Namangan State Technical University, IT Park

metric.l: enterprises with pilot AI solutions / year

items.title: “Digital Employee” programme — a service to digitalize a small business in 30 days
items.what: A standard package for neighbourhood and district entrepreneurs (shops, eateries, clinics, training centres) covering a Telegram bot, online ordering, CRM, electronic reporting and automated social media marketing. The service is delivered by students trained at the technopark.
how: Define “Starter”, “Standard” and “Premium” packages with fixed prices
Engage entrepreneurs through khokim assistants and the regional office of the Youth Affairs Agency
Add every completed project to the student's portfolio
items.result: At least 200 small businesses digitalized per year, and more than 100 young people earning freelance income.

items.title: Launch “Namangan Challenge” — an open innovation platform for regional enterprises' technology challenges
items.what: The survey notes the absence of a unified registry of enterprises' technology challenges and orders. On the platform, enterprises post a challenge (e.g. cutting energy use, recycling waste, replacing imported parts) and a reward; young people and startups propose solutions. The winning solution is prototyped on technopark equipment.
how: Connect enterprises to the platform via the regional khokimiyat and the regional office of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry
Update the challenge registry monthly and publish it openly
Make a pilot contract between the enterprise and the technopark a mandatory step for winning solutions
items.result: A steady order pipeline for the technopark and startup ideas grounded in real problems for young people.
items.partners: Technopark, regional khokimiyat, Chamber of Commerce and Industry

metric.l: enterprise challenges in the open registry

items.title: Establish an industrial IoT and digital twin laboratory
items.what: Develop and install low-cost sensor kits for textile, food and cold-storage facilities to remotely monitor equipment condition, electricity and gas consumption, temperature and humidity.
how: Use existing 3D printers and robotics equipment to produce sensor housings and control units
Formalize joint laboratory status with Namangan State Technical University
Introduce a shared-savings contract model with enterprises based on energy savings achieved
items.result: Energy consumption at enterprises reduced by up to 10–20%, and a locally manufactured IoT product line.
items.partners: Technopark, Namangan State Technical University, enterprises

items.title: Launch the “AI Teacher” retraining programme for school teachers
items.what: A 72-hour hands-on course for the region's computer science, physics and technology teachers on AI tools, robotics and 3D modelling. Each teacher opens a technopark-oriented club at their school and refers gifted students to the technopark.
how: Select teachers under an agreement with the regional Department of Preschool and School Education
Award certificates to graduates and work towards recognizing the course as professional development hours
Hold an annual regional “Best AI Teacher” competition
items.result: A continuous pipeline of young talent from school level; a network of technopark “ambassador teachers” in every district.

directions.title: Specialization in Regional Industry
directions.desc: Textiles, agritech, crafts, green and assistive technologies.

items.title: Open the “TextileTech Lab” for textiles and light industry
items.what: Prototyping services for textiles and garment-making, Namangan Region's leading industry: digital fashion design (3D virtual patterns and samples), laser cutting, embroidery and labelling, and smart fabrics.
how: Sign partnership memoranda with Textgroup and other textile clusters in the region
Hold a “Design Sprint” for young designers — a two-week competition to create a collection to order
Help enterprises introduce export-compliant product labels and QR-code traceability
items.result: Shorter new-product development cycles for the industry and jobs for young designers and technologists.

items.title: “Namangan AgroTech Testbed” — a field-testing site for agricultural technologies
items.what: In partnership with farms and horticulture clusters, field-test smart irrigation, soil moisture sensors, drone-based crop monitoring and monitoring of fruit and vegetable storage. Namangan's floriculture and horticulture traditions are taken into account.
how: Sign test-site agreements with 1–2 farms
Keep a protocol and results report for every trial — building a pilot testing and validation system at the same time
Develop a leasing or subscription model to deliver successful solutions to farmers
items.result: Field-validated test results for prototypes and first customers for agritech startups.

items.title: Digitalize crafts and jewellery — launch the “CraftTech” direction
items.what: Enhance regional crafts — Chust knives, skullcap-making, pottery, woodcarving — with modern design using 3D scanning, laser engraving and jewellery equipment. Prepare advance customers and a team of young artisans for the 6 jewellery machines now being installed.
how: Launch a “master–apprentice + digital design” programme with the Craftsmen's Association
Help set up photography, product descriptions and payment systems for export via international e-commerce platforms
Open a 3D-printed wax model service for jewellery
items.result: The regional brand reaches foreign markets; income-generating home-based jobs for women and young people.

items.title: “Green Technologies” — recycling plastic waste into 3D printer filament and finished products
items.what: Using the existing thermoplastic equipment and 3D printers, shred plastic waste collected from neighbourhoods, schools and enterprises, turn it into filament and pellets, and produce building tiles, furniture fittings and educational supplies.
how: Run a “Hand in plastic — get a bonus” campaign in neighbourhoods through youth leaders
Sign recycling partnership agreements with the khokimiyat and sanitation companies
Cut costs by producing consumables for the technopark's 3D printers in-house
items.result: Lower consumables costs, a ready business model for eco-startups, and a contribution to the region's environment.

items.title: Open an assistive technologies direction for persons with disabilities (3D-printed prostheses, adapted devices)
items.what: Use 3D printers to develop hand prostheses, orthoses, tactile learning aids for the visually impaired and adapted mobility devices. With its strong social value, this direction provides a solid basis for attracting international grants and sponsors.
how: Compile a register of people in need together with medical institutions and social protection bodies
Establish a procedure for obtaining a physician's opinion for every product
Set up a dedicated grant and sponsorship fund for social startups
items.result: A local solution several times cheaper than imported prostheses, and a stronger social reputation for the technopark.

metric.l: adapted solutions for people in need

directions.title: Startup Ecosystem and Investment
directions.desc: Startup Studio, business angels, first-order procurement, corporate accelerators.

items.title: Transition the technopark to a “Startup Studio” (venture builder) model
items.what: Rather than merely receiving ideas, the technopark itself identifies market problems, assembles teams and takes them through prototyping and legal registration to their first customer. In return, an agreed share of the startup's revenue or equity (royalty or stake) returns to the technopark, as provided by law.
how: Develop the legal basis for the model (royalty agreement, equity stake or other mechanism) in agreement with the Innovative Development Agency
Each year, launch 5 studio startups based on the 5 most in-demand challenges on the “Namangan Challenge” platform
Assign an experienced entrepreneur to each studio startup as a “founder-mentor”
items.result: Companies that reach the market instead of projects stuck at the idea stage, and long-term revenue for the technopark.

items.title: “Namangan Angels” — establish a local business angel club
items.what: Unite successful regional entrepreneurs in a club that makes small investments in startups. A closed pitch session is held at the technopark every month, and club members co-invest as a syndicate.
how: Recruit 15–20 entrepreneurs to the club in the first phase
Prepare a set of standard investment documents (term sheet, equity split, convertible note)
Channel the best projects to follow-on investment with UzVC and other venture funds
items.result: Access to private capital beyond state grants, with at least 8–10 startups funded per year.

items.title: “First Order” mechanism — pilot procurement of startup products by public organizations
items.what: A startup's biggest barrier is its first customer. The regional and district khokimiyats, utilities, schools and hospitals will place at least 5–10 pilot orders with technopark startups each year (e.g. smart lighting, queue management systems, e-accounting solutions).
how: Set the pilot procurement budget limit and selection procedure within public procurement law
Have the organization issue a formal assessment (letter of recommendation) at the end of each pilot
Scale solutions with positive assessments to other districts
items.result: A real portfolio and revenue for startups, and better-quality public services.

items.title: Launch “Corporate Accelerator” programmes with major enterprises
items.what: Each major enterprise (Nambiotest, Textgroup, Mexmash and others) funds one three-month acceleration cohort per year tailored to its needs. The enterprise sets the challenge, the technopark provides the teams and methodology, and the winning teams sign contracts with the enterprise.
how: Agree a separate partnership programme and budget with each enterprise
Hold a Demo Day with the enterprise's leadership at the end of each accelerator
Give the enterprise the option to adopt the solution in-house or acquire the startup (M&A)
items.result: Enterprises' innovation spending flows through the technopark; young people gain a direct path into industry.

items.title: Hold quarterly “Namangan Hack Week” hackathons and an annual “Fergana Valley Startup Week” forum
items.what: Each quarter has its own theme (AI, AgroTech, TextileTech, GreenTech). The annual forum brings together the Andijan, Fergana and Namangan technoparks, investors and international experts, positioning Namangan as the startup hub of the valley.
how: Build the hackathon prize fund from sponsoring enterprises
Admit winning teams directly to InnoX or the Startup Studio programme
Livestream the forum and publish the results as an open report
items.result: More than 500 young people engaged each year, and a flow of new teams and investors.

items.title: “Namangan Global Mentors” — engaging Namangan professionals at home and abroad as mentors
items.what: The technopark currently has only 2 mentors. Unite compatriots from Namangan who work at international companies or have succeeded in science and business into an online mentoring network.
how: Build a mentor database and schedule at least 2 online sessions per month for each startup
Non-financial incentives for mentors: “Honorary Mentor” status, khokimiyat letters of appreciation, recognition at events
Invite mentors to Namangan once a year as part of the forum
items.result: Mentor numbers grow from 2 to at least 30, giving startups international expertise and connections.

directions.title: Talent Development and Youth Outreach
directions.desc: Fellowship, international certification, Mobile FabLab, Women in Tech, startup as a thesis.

items.title: “Technopark Fellowship” — a 6-month paid internship programme
items.what: Gifted university graduates and senior students spend 6 months at the technopark working on a real project commissioned by an enterprise. The stipend is co-funded by the enterprise and the technopark, and the best fellows are hired by the enterprise at the end.
how: Admit 20–30 young people per cohort through an open competition
Require the commissioning enterprise to cover at least half of the stipend
Agree with universities to recognize the programme as a professional internship or graduation thesis
items.result: Employment for graduates, job-ready talent for enterprises, and a network of corporate partners for the technopark.

items.title: Establish an international certification and testing centre at the technopark
items.what: Make it possible to take internationally recognized certification exams in 3D modelling, engineering design, networking, cloud services and programming in Namangan itself. Today, young people have to travel to Tashkent.
how: Apply to international exam providers for official test centre status
Offer paid exam preparation courses using technopark equipment
Direct graduates of “One Million Coders” and IT Park training programmes to certification
items.result: Young people more competitive on the global labour market, and a sustainable service revenue for the technopark.

items.title: Launch a “Mobile FabLab” for the districts — a technopark lab on wheels
items.what: A specially equipped vehicle carries a 3D printer, robotics kits, laptops and VR headsets. On a set schedule, the mobile lab visits schools and colleges in Chust, Pop, Kosonsoy, Uchkurgan, Davlatobod and other districts, running hands-on sessions and idea selection.
how: Equip the mobile lab through an international grant or a sponsoring enterprise
Approve a schedule of at least 2 visits per month to each district
Admit gifted young people identified in the districts to the technopark's core programmes
items.result: The technopark's reach extends from the city to the entire region, with equal opportunity for rural youth.

items.title: Launch the “Women in Tech Namangan” programme for girls and women
items.what: A dedicated track to engage girls in programming, digital design, AI and entrepreneurship: mentoring by successful women entrepreneurs, remote work skills, and a separate competition for women-founded startups.
how: Recruit participants together with women's committees and mahalla activists
Schedule sessions at convenient times and in convenient formats for girls (blended online/offline)
Submit joint applications to international organizations' gender equality grant programmes
items.result: The share of girls among technopark participants reaches at least 30%.

items.title: Scale up the “Startup as a Thesis” practice across Namangan's universities
items.what: Together with Namangan State University, Namangan State Technical University and other universities, establish a system allowing students to defend a startup project and prototype built at the technopark as their graduation thesis.
how: Develop joint regulations with universities, including defence criteria and procedures
Include a technopark representative and entrepreneurs on the defence committee
Give students who defend a startup priority admission to the Startup Studio programme
items.result: Research no longer gathers dust on the shelf but becomes a practical product; universities meet their startup KPIs.

directions.title: Intellectual Property and Technology Transfer
directions.desc: IP and technology transfer office, independent technical review and TRL assessment.

items.title: Establish an intellectual property and technology transfer office at the technopark
items.what: The survey reports no results in technology transfer. The office will provide free advice to young people and researchers on registering inventions, utility models, industrial designs and trademarks, and will arrange licensing of developments to enterprises.
how: Sign a memorandum of cooperation with the competent IP authorities
Make an IP protection assessment a mandatory step for every prototype built at the technopark
Establish a transparent licensing revenue split between the author, the technopark and the university
items.result: Applications for at least 15 IP objects per year, and additional revenue from licensing.

items.title: Set up an independent “Technical Review and Validation Board” for prototypes
items.what: The survey shows there are no pilot test protocols or independent expert reviews. The board, made up of university professors, industry engineers and investors, will assess each prototype by Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
how: Approve a single assessment form and criteria based on the TRL scale
Review the 9 mock-up-stage prototypes first and draw up a roadmap for each
Present projects with positive reviews to investors and enterprises
items.result: Prototypes in production grow from 2 to at least 10; a reliable data base for investors.

directions.title: Own-Revenue Growth Model
directions.desc: Maker membership, international grants project office, technopark brand and online store.

items.title: Introduce “maker membership” and hourly equipment access with online booking
items.what: Young people, artisans and small entrepreneurs use 3D printers, lasers and other equipment on a monthly membership or hourly basis. Equipment availability is managed through an online schedule, which also allows utilization to be measured precisely.
how: Set tiered pricing for students, startups and commercial clients
Introduce mandatory short safety training and a user permit before equipment use
Keep a monthly utilization report for each piece of equipment
items.result: Higher equipment utilization, a small but steady revenue stream, and systematic safety assurance.

items.title: Establish a “Project Office” to work with international grants and donor organizations
items.what: Prepare regular applications on behalf of the technopark and its startups to grant programmes of international organizations and development agencies (EU, UN agencies, German, Korean and Japanese development agencies and others) focused on youth, innovation, the green economy and digitalization.
how: Recruit or train 1–2 English-speaking grant managers
Maintain a calendar of open grant calls and submit at least 2 applications per quarter
Use grants won to fund the Mobile FabLab, assistive technologies and green technologies directions
items.result: An additional funding source with no burden on the state budget.

items.title: Create the “Made in Namangan Technopark” brand and online store for technopark products
items.what: Products made by the technopark and its residents (3D souvenirs, acrylic décor, IoT devices, crafts) are sold under a single brand via marketplaces, social media and the technopark's own online store. The brand also raises public awareness of the technopark's work.
how: Develop a unified brand, packaging and quality standard
Sign annual corporate gift contracts with public and private organizations
Return a set share of sales revenue to youth teams
items.result: Additional revenue and visibility for the technopark, and a sales channel for young makers.

directions.title: Governance, Partnership and Transparency
directions.desc: Valley technopark consortium, IT Park integration, open KPI dashboard, supervisory board.

items.title: Form a unified, specialization-based network (consortium) of Fergana Valley youth technoparks
items.what: The Andijan, Fergana and Namangan technoparks each specialize in their strongest field and refer orders to one another. For example, automotive parts orders go to Andijan, while textile, AI and crafts orders go to Namangan. Equipment, mentor and investor databases are shared across the network.
how: Sign a memorandum of cooperation between the technoparks with the support of the Innovative Development Agency
Create a single online catalogue of each technopark's equipment and specialization
Host the annual valley forum on a rotating basis
items.result: Duplicate equipment purchases are avoided, order volumes grow, and Namangan becomes the leading centre in its fields.
items.partners: Andijan, Fergana and Namangan technoparks, Innovative Development Agency

items.title: Integrate with IT Park's Namangan branch — a fast track for technopark startups to IT Park residency
items.what: Once digital and AI startups at the technopark mature, simplify document preparation and review so they can access IT Park residency benefits. This also partly addresses the survey finding that mature startups show little interest in staying at the technopark.
how: Sign a joint cooperation programme with IT Park's regional branch
Establish a procedure for recommending technopark graduates for residency
Hold a joint Demo Day every quarter
items.result: Startups remain in the region at the growth stage and benefit from tax incentives.

items.title: Introduce an open online KPI dashboard of technopark performance
items.what: Indicators such as the number of startups, young people engaged, order volume, equipment utilization, own revenue and prototypes in production are published monthly on an open online dashboard. This fills the gaps the survey flagged as “no verified data provided”.
how: Keep all orders, contracts and projects in a single electronic registry
Approve 10–15 core KPIs in agreement with the Innovative Development Agency
Update indicators monthly and report to the khokimiyat quarterly
items.result: Transparent technopark operations, trust from investors and partners, and results-based management.

items.title: Establish a Supervisory (Advisory) Board of industry, university and business representatives at the technopark
items.what: The board meets quarterly to review the technopark's directions, partnerships and results, convey enterprises' needs directly and provide strategic recommendations.
how: Include representatives of 3–4 major enterprises, 2–3 universities, IT Park, entrepreneurs and youth on the board
Establish a procedure for incorporating board recommendations into the technopark's annual work plan
Attract sponsorship and investment through board members
items.result: The technopark's directions continuously adapt to market demand, and its partnership network expands.
